html:
The Maijuna are a small Indigenous people of the northern Peruvian Amazon, living on the Algodón, Yanayacu and Sucusari rivers, which feed the Napo and Putumayo. Outsiders long called them Orejones, "big ears", for the wooden discs they wore in their earlobes.

They speak a Western Tucanoan language, related to that of the Secoya and Siona to the north. Colonial missions, epidemics and the rubber boom around 1900 cut their numbers to a few hundred. In 2015 Peru created the Maijuna-Kichwa Regional Conservation Area, shared with their Napo Kichwa neighbours, to protect their forest from logging and a planned road.
